text.p: Fiorentina had their appeal against a two-match home ban turned down by UEFA on Friday but had suspensions to two players reduced.

Fiorentina had been ordered to play their next two European matches 500 kms from Florence following disturbances when they played Barcelona in the second leg of their European Cup Winners' Cup semifinal second leg on April 24.
Barcelona coach Bobby Robson was hit by a bottle while players Sergi Barjuan and Ivan de la Pena were hit by other objects thrown by Fiorentina fans.

UEFA's Control and Disciplinary Committee reduced the suspension of Fiorentina's Portuguese captain Rui Costa for insulting the referee from four games to three and that of his Swedish team mate Stefan Schwarz from three to one.

UEFA also reduced a fine on Porto from 100,000 Swiss francs ($69,700) to 30,000. The fine was imposed because of crowd disturbances at the Portuguese club's European Cup quarter-final second leg against England's Manchester United in Oporto on March 19. ($ = 1.434 Swiss Francs)
